title: Hilbert 14: Sharpness of the Degree Bound β(Sₙ) = n
description: The parent (hilbert-14-oq-02) proves the UPPER bound of the optimal-degree question for the symmetric group Sₙ: the invariant ring R[x₁,…,xₙ]^{Sₙ} is generated by the n elementary symmetric polynomials e₁,…,eₙ, with eₖ homogeneous of degree k, so β(Sₙ) ≤ n. This entry proves the complementary LOWER bound, i.e. that the bound is SHARP: the top generator eₙ is transcendental over the subalgebra R[e₁,…,e_{n-1}] generated by the lower elementary symmetric polynomials, hence eₙ ∉ R[e₁,…,e_{n-1}]. So eₙ is a genuinely new generator at degree exactly n and the generating degree cannot be lowered: β(Sₙ) ≥ n, hence β(Sₙ) = n. The argument is short and structural: a member of an algebraically independent family is transcendental over the subalgebra generated by the others (AlgebraicIndependent.transcendental_adjoin), applied to the top index. 0 axioms.

SCOPE: this proves the SHARPNESS (lower bound β(Sₙ) ≥ n) for the symmetric group Sₙ, complementing the parent's upper bound β(Sₙ) ≤ n. The non-membership is stated for the lower ELEMENTARY symmetric family; a fully general 'no generating set in degrees < n' statement (over ALL degree-<n invariants) would additionally require that every invariant of degree < n is a polynomial in e₁,…,e_{n-1}, which is true but not formalized here — see open questions.

overview.historicalContext: Hilbert's 14th problem concerns finite generation of invariant rings R[V]^G. A natural refinement (the parent's OQ-02) asks for the OPTIMAL degree bound β(G): the smallest D such that R[V]^G is generated by invariants of degree ≤ D. For the symmetric group Sₙ acting on R[x₁,…,xₙ], the Fundamental Theorem of Symmetric Polynomials shows the invariants are freely generated by the elementary symmetric polynomials e₁,…,eₙ with eₖ of degree k, so β(Sₙ) ≤ n. Proving β(Sₙ) = n requires the complementary lower bound: that one genuinely cannot generate with elements of smaller degree. The cleanest witness is the top generator eₙ = x₁⋯xₙ itself: because e₁,…,eₙ are algebraically independent, eₙ is transcendental over R[e₁,…,e_{n-1}] and in particular is not a polynomial in the lower elementary symmetric polynomials. Since the lower ones all have degree ≤ n-1, the generating degree cannot drop below n. This entry formalizes that lower bound.
overview.problemStatement: For the symmetric group Sₙ (|σ| = n = m+1), prove the sharpness of the optimal degree bound: the top elementary symmetric polynomial eₙ is transcendental over the subalgebra R[e₁,…,e_{n-1}] generated by the lower elementary symmetric polynomials, hence eₙ ∉ R[e₁,…,e_{n-1}]. Conclude β(Sₙ) ≥ n, so β(Sₙ) = n with the parent's β(Sₙ) ≤ n.
overview.proofStrategy: Re-establish self-contained that e₁,…,eₙ are algebraically independent (esymm_algebraicIndependent, via injectivity of esymmAlgHom through the subalgebra inclusion). Index the family over Fin (m+1) by i ↦ e_{i+1}. Apply AlgebraicIndependent.transcendental_adjoin with s = the first m indices (Set.range Fin.castSucc) and i = the top index Fin.last m: a member of an algebraically independent family is transcendental over the subalgebra generated by the others. Identify the image of the lower indices with the set of lower elementary symmetric polynomials (Set.range_comp + Fin.coe_castSucc) and the top family value with eₙ (Fin.val_last), yielding eₙ transcendental over R[e₁,…,e_{n-1}]. Non-membership follows because every element of a subalgebra is algebraic over it (isAlgebraic_algebraMap contradicts transcendence). The capstone packages eₙ's symmetry, exact degree n homogeneity, and non-membership.
keyInsights: Sharpness of β(Sₙ) = n is a transcendence statement: the top generator eₙ is transcendental over the algebra generated by the lower elementary symmetric polynomials, not merely outside it.

The whole lower bound is a one-line specialisation of a general fact — a member of an algebraically independent family is transcendental over the subalgebra generated by the others (AlgebraicIndependent.transcendental_adjoin) — applied to the top index of e₁,…,eₙ.
The parent supplied exactly the hypothesis needed: algebraic independence of e₁,…,eₙ (its 'optimal number' theorem) is precisely what powers the 'optimal degree lower bound' here.

Transcendence over a subalgebra B implies non-membership in B, because every element of B is algebraic over B (isAlgebraic_algebraMap); this turns the abstract transcendence into the concrete eₙ ∉ R[e₁,…,e_{n-1}].

Because the lower elementary symmetric polynomials all have degree < n while eₙ has degree exactly n and escapes their subalgebra, the optimal generating degree cannot be reduced below n — the bound β(Sₙ) ≤ n is attained.

conclusion.summary: The optimal-degree bound for the symmetric group is sharp: β(Sₙ) = n. The parent established the upper bound β(Sₙ) ≤ n (the invariants R[x₁,…,xₙ]^{Sₙ} are generated by e₁,…,eₙ with eₖ of degree k); this entry supplies the matching lower bound β(Sₙ) ≥ n by showing the top elementary symmetric polynomial eₙ is transcendental over the subalgebra R[e₁,…,e_{n-1}] generated by the lower ones, hence eₙ ∉ R[e₁,…,e_{n-1}]. Since all lower generators have degree < n, eₙ is a genuinely new generator at degree exactly n and the generating degree cannot be reduced.
conclusion.implications: The argument exhibits the sharpness of a degree bound as a transcendence statement rather than a counting one: algebraic independence of a generating family is precisely what forces its top member out of the subalgebra generated by the rest (AlgebraicIndependent.transcendental_adjoin), and transcendence over a subalgebra implies non-membership because every element of a subalgebra is algebraic over it. This is a clean template for lower bounds on β(G) whenever the invariant ring is a polynomial algebra on known generators — the same move applies to any free invariant ring (e.g. complex reflection groups, by Chevalley–Shephard–Todd), pinning β(G) to the top fundamental-invariant degree. It also closes the β(Sₙ) question exactly, complementing Noether's degree bound β(G) ≤ |G| for finite groups, which for Sₙ would only give the far weaker β(Sₙ) ≤ n!.
openQuestions: Strengthen the lower bound from the elementary-symmetric family to ALL invariants of degree < n: prove that every symmetric polynomial of total degree < n lies in R[e₁,…,e_{n-1}], so that no generating set consisting of elements of degree < n can exist (upgrading the witness β(Sₙ) ≥ n to a statement quantified over all degree-<n generating families).
